title: Load Ledger: end-to-end benchmarking harness and customer sign-off flow for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Aisha Fernandez
description:
Purpose:
Build a reproducible, auditable benchmarking and validation harness ("Load Ledger") for Dedicated Capacity SLAs that can: capture per-request token latency distributions, validate autoscaling policy behaviour under mixed workloads, and produce a customer-facing validation report used for onboarding and sign-off.

Goals:
- Provide a single binary/config set that deploys test clients, traffic controllers, and collectors across a dedicated pool.
- Measure median/95/99/99.9 tail latencies, throughput, and token-cost tradeoffs across representative model families (Llama2, Mistral, RW-2 variants).
- Validate autoscaling policies: fixed-step, target-utilization, and predictive-burst.
- Generate a signed PDF report for customer acceptance with pass/fail checks and raw CSV artifacts.
- Integrate with CI so we can gate capacity changes and release upgrades.

Scope and non-goals:
- Includes load generation, synthetic & real-customer replay (anonymized), metric aggregation, and sign-off templates.
- Does NOT include workload synthesis research for new model architectures (separate task).

Design decisions and trade-offs so far:
1) Orchestration: use a Kubernetes Job + distributed controller vs. ephemeral serverless runners. We chose K8s Job for determinism and easier networking hooks (consistent with Dedicated infra).
2) Traffic shaping: implement a "scenario descriptor" JSON that describes arrival process (Poisson, burst, conversational burst with KV-cache warmup). This lets us reproduce customer patterns exactly.
3) Metric collection: rely on our observability SDK to emit per-token and per-request traces to Tempo/Prometheus, but capture high-resolution samples locally to avoid sampling bias. Storing compressed CSVs to S3 for audits.
4) Customer report: include deterministic acceptance criteria (e.g., p99 latency below threshold for 95% of run windows) to avoid vague "looks good" outcomes.

Benchmark methodology (high level):
- Warmup phase: ramp 0->target over configurable duration while issuing KV-cache priming sequences.
- Steady-state: maintain target arrival rate for 30m windows, collect per-window metrics.
- Burst validation: introduce scheduled bursts that exceed target by X% for Ys to exercise autoscaler.
- Failure modes: run a simulated node loss to validate graceful reroute and capacity fallback.
- Repeatability: each scenario is seeded; all randomness (client IDs, prompt prefixes) deterministically derived from seed.

Acceptance criteria for customer sign-off (template):
- Functional: all request types succeed with <1% error rate.
- Latency: rolling 30m window p99 <= agreed threshold; 99.9 percentile outliers documented and justified.
- Throughput: achieved 95% of committed tokens/sec for 90% of the test windows.
- Autoscale: recovery time after induced load spike meets contract (e.g., < 2x the SLO window).
- Observability: all traces and raw CSVs available and linked in final report.

Deliverables:
- Load Ledger harness repo with: scenario descriptors, k8s manifests, controller binary, aggregator, and report generator.
- CI job that runs basic smoke scenarios on PRs to the runtime and Dedicated infra stacks.
- Customer sign-off PDF template and checklist stored in Drive (link below).
- Runbook for operators describing how to execute a validation lab and interpret results.

Integration points and links:
- Design spec (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/docs/dedicated/load-ledger-spec (draft)
- GitHub prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/load-ledger (WIP PR #42)
- Dashboard prototype: /console/dedicated/bench-reports/load-ledger (internal)

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Observability sampling masks hot tails. Mitigation: write ungated local sample capture and cross-validate with production traces.
- Risk: Customer workloads vary wildly and replaying causes PII exposure. Mitigation: require PII scrub step and only allow anonymized trace ingestion for replays.
- Risk: Test-induced failures affect other tenants in shared infra. Mitigation: ensure Dedicated labs run in isolated reserved pools and implement kill-switch to immediately stop traffic.

Next milestones and timeline:
- 2026-02-20: prototype harness that runs a single model family and emits CSVs (done)
- 2026-02-28: scenario descriptor schema finalized and reviewed (complete)
- 2026-03-05: autoscale policy test harness integrated (in progress)
- 2026-03-12: customer sign-off report generator complete and first internal dry-run
- 2026-03-20: run an onboarding validation with first pilot customer

Notes for reviewers:
- Please check the scenario descriptor schema for expressiveness and missing knobs (context length distributions, stop-token distributions, session churn).
- We plan to reuse parts of ENG-4721's load tooling but avoid synchronizing step schedules to prevent correlated spikes across tests.

Attached artifacts and links (for audit):

- Drive sign-off template: https://drive.redwood.ai/forms/load-ledger-signoff-template
- Operator runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Load+Ledger+Runbook
